title: Complex Number
notes: **Complex Number:** This topic covers the fundamental concepts of complex number in the mathematics curriculum.
Understanding complex number is essential for solving problems and building higher-level mathematical skills.
Key definitions and theorems related to complex number should be memorized and practiced regularly.
confusion: i = √(-1), so i² = -1. But √(-4) ≠ 2i — it equals 2i (principal square root). Be careful with √(a)·√(b) = √(ab) — this fails for negative a,b.
The modulus |z| is ALWAYS non-negative. |z| = √(a²+b²), not √(a²-b²).
Conjugate z̄ changes the sign of the IMAGINARY part only: if z=a+bi, then z̄=a-bi.
practice: Find the modulus and argument of z = -1+i√3.
If z = 2(cos π/6 + i sin π/6), find z³ using De Moivre's theorem.
universalFacts: Cardano first encountered complex numbers while solving cubic equations in 1545, though he didn't understand them fully.
Gauss gave the first rigorous treatment of complex numbers and proved the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra.
Complex numbers are essential in electrical engineering (AC circuits), quantum mechanics, and signal processing.
